messages.author: 424bb31dbf8d29df
messages.subject: My model is not identified HELP
parts:
Hey guys! Can anyone tell what is wrong with my model?
R is saying that it may not be identified!

This is what im running: 
modelo <-'
AcquiringKnowledge =~ A2 + A3 + A4 + A6
FanIdentification =~ F1 + F2 + F3 + F4 + F5 + F6 + F7 
UncertaintyOfOutcome =~ U2 + U5 + U6 + U7
Spectatorship =~ AcquiringKnowledge + FanIdentification + UncertaintyOfOutcome

Spectatorship ~ AcquiringKnowledge + FanIdentification + UncertaintyOfOutcome
'
fit <- sem(modelo, data=V1)
summary(fit, standardized=TRUE)

It should look like the image, but not whit those numbers. Im having trouble running the regression.

messages.author: 12fdd832cacb825e
messages.subject: Re: My model is not identified HELP
parts:
Otavio,

You have spectatorship both measured by (i.e., causing) the other
factors and regressed on (i.e., caused by) the other factors. You need
to remove whichever of the last two lines is inappropriate for your
theory.

messages.author: 12fdd832cacb825e
messages.subject: Re: My model is not identified HELP
parts:
Ok, you just described two different things.

=~ in lavaan means "measured by"
~ means "caused by"

"a latent variable of the other factors" is a second-order factor, and uses =~
"to what degree each factor contributes to explain the spectatorship."

is a regression relation, and uses ~, but "Spectatorship" has to exist
somewhere to be explained.

I suggest you spend some time with some materials that introduce you
to SEM to get at the basic terminology, which will make it much easier
for people to help when you're stuck. There's a lot out there,
including entire textbooks--Rex Kline's is often recommended.
